title: Loch Modan
body: Loch Modan is a highland of green hills and pine woods east of Dun Morogh, held by the dwarves of Ironforge and named for the great lake at its heart. At the loch's northern end the Stonewrought Dam holds back its waters, one of the grandest works ever raised. In the Second War the orcs of the Horde overran these hills, and the dwarves won them back once the war was done. Today the region is thinly guarded. Many of Ironforge's soldiers have marched off to distant fronts, leaving a handful of mountaineers in the guard towers and the town of Thelsamar to hold the line. They have plenty to hold it against: Stonesplinter troggs boiling up out of the earth, Tunnel Rat kobolds in the western hills, Mo'grosh ogres in the northeast, Dragonmaw orcs pressing into the pass of Dun Algaz, and Dark Iron saboteurs creeping toward the dam itself.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Loch_Modan (loch gave the region its name; Horde overran it in the Second War, dwarves reclaimed it)
quest 1558 description (dam one of the biggest things anyone has made)
quests 224, 237, 267 (reserves called to the front, troggs tunneling up)

Wiki mention of pre-Cataclysm earthquakes left out on purpose (tied to the Cataclysm lead-up). Council of Three Hammers not used (Cataclysm era).

title: Valley of Kings
body: In the southwestern corner of Loch Modan, where the road from Dun Morogh comes through the mountains, two colossal stone dwarves stand watch over the pass into the southlands. They depict King Madoran Bronzebeard and King Khardros Wildhammer, raised in their honor by their sons after both kings had died, as a warning to any who would attack the dwarven realms and a reminder of the price the Dark Irons paid for their treachery. Nearby stands the southern guard tower, where Captain Rugelfuss and his regiment guard the gate and wage war on the troggs in the hills. Farther south, a locked gate leads to the Searing Gorge, and Mountaineer Pebblebitty refuses entry to nearly everyone who asks.
sources: page_text 1929-1930, in-game book War of the Three Hammers (gameobject 175739): the sons of Madoran and Khardros commissioned the statues, which guard the pass into the southlands as a warning and a reminder of the Dark Irons' price
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Valley_of_Kings (statues of Madoran and Khardros commissioned by their sons, guard the pass into the southlands; cites History of Warcraft)

title: Stonesplinter Valley
body: In the mountains of southwestern Loch Modan lies Stonesplinter Valley, the heartland of the Stonesplinter troggs. These brutish creatures were unearthed from caverns far below by the dwarves' own digging, and they have been tunneling up from every crevice ever since. Scouts and seers, skullthumpers, bonesnappers and shamans swarm across the slopes, and deep within the valley their chieftain Grawmug keeps his lair behind his two hulking guards, Gnasher and Brawler. The troggs make no secret of their ambitions. Their battle cries proclaim that the Loch now belongs to the Stonesplinter tribe.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Stonesplinter_Valley (southwestern Loch Modan, Grawmug deep in the valley)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Loch_Modan (troggs unearthed from caves below by the dwarven digs)

title: Grizzlepaw Ridge
body: Grizzlepaw Ridge is a wooded height rising south of Thelsamar, with Stonesplinter Valley spread out to the west. It is bear country. Grizzled black bears and great patriarchs roam its slopes, and somewhere in the hills above Thelsamar lies the lair of Ol' Sooty, a large bear that the hunters of the Farstrider Lodge once set out to bring down, and none of them had any luck. Now and then the old bear comes down from its den to maul anyone foolish enough to provoke it.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Grizzlepaw_Ridge (south of Thelsamar, east of Stonesplinter Valley, bears, Ol' Sooty comes down to attack those who provoke him)
DB spawns in area 936: Grizzled Black Bear, Black Bear Patriarch, Ol' Sooty 1225

title: Thelsamar
body: Thelsamar is the chief town of Loch Modan, a cluster of stout dwarven houses on the western side of the loch, just off the road that runs between Dun Morogh and the Wetlands. Magistrate Bluntnose governs it, the Thelsamar Mountaineers patrol its lanes, and the Explorers' League keeps a branch house here, where Jern Hornhelm serves as contact for the digs. The Stoutlager Inn promises full tankards and long stories, and the town is famous for its blood sausages, with hungry workers from the excavation crowding in after a hard day's work. Thorgrum Borrelson keeps the gryphon roost and swears no faster gryphons fly anywhere in the Eastern Kingdoms.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Thelsamar (west side of Loch Modan, road toward Dun Morogh and the Wetlands, Stoutlager Inn, Thelsamar Mountaineers)

title: Silver Stream Mine
body: North of Thelsamar, the Silver Stream Mine was once a rich source of silver for the dwarves of Ironforge. When its veins ran dry, the Miners' League turned the old tunnels into a storage depot, stacking crates of tools and gear in its galleries. Now Tunnel Rat kobolds have moved in and are pawing through good dwarven tools, and the mountaineers are itching for the order to clear them out. The League would rather its gear were carried out first, before the soldiers start breaking things. Among the vermin skulks a rarely seen kobold called Grizlak.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Silver_Stream_Mine (bountiful source of silver, storage depot)

title: Algaz Station
body: Just east of the North Gate Pass from Dun Morogh stands Algaz Station, the northern guard tower of Loch Modan, a dwarven outpost manned by mountaineers and named for the pass of Dun Algaz beyond it. From the top of the tower Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike keeps watch, a member of a proud and wealthy clan with discerning tastes: he has commissioned an axe from a smith in Stormwind and ordered a shield from Furen Longbeard, a dwarven armorsmith he admires in that city's dwarven district. The armorer Gothor Brumn serves those passing through, and the kobold-infested Silver Stream Mine lies a short way to the east.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Algaz_Station (east of North Gate Pass, south of Dun Algaz, takes its name from it, mountaineers, Stormpike, Gothor Brumn)

title: Dun Algaz
body: Dun Algaz is the mountain pass that carries the road north out of Loch Modan into the Wetlands and on to Menethil Harbor, the Alliance port and stronghold on the coast. Its stronghold has a long and bloody past. When the Horde was driven south across the Thandol Valley in the Second War, Dun Algaz became its last hold, and the assault Anduin Lothar ordered against it failed. Now the orcs have returned. Dragonmaw warriors from the Wetlands have pushed into the pass, threatening to cut Loch Modan off from Menethil, and Mountaineer Rockgar is calling for volunteers to break through.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Dun_Algaz (Second War: orcs retreated south across the Thandol Valley, Lothar's assault failed, last hold; original WoW: Dragonmaw overran the post)
DB spawn: Mountaineer Rockgar 1342 in area 837

title: Stonewrought Dam
body: The Stonewrought Dam spans the northern end of the loch, a vast wall of stone holding back its waters, which spill down a great waterfall toward the Wetlands below. It is counted among the greatest works the dwarves ever built, and even an orphan of Stormwind begs to be taken to see it. Far beneath it, at the very foot of the falls, grows the musquash root, found nowhere else. Today it is the Dark Iron clan that threatens the dam, with sappers lurking on its eastern ramp and insurgents swimming at its base. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII oversees the dam with a small company of mountaineers, much of its security detail having been called away to the front.
sources: quest 1558 description and reward text (Children's Week: huge dam, big waterfall, rushing water)
quest 335 description (Musquash Root found only at the base of the falls far beneath the dam)

title: The Loch
body: The loch that gives the land its name is the largest body of water in all of Khaz Modan, its waters held high by the Stonewrought Dam. Islands rise from its cold waters and the crocolisks have claimed them, making the loch famous among hunters who come for skins and meat. Threshadons glide through its depths. Fishermen ply their trade along the western shore northeast of Thelsamar, and the road to the excavation runs south from town along the curve of the shore, the route the porters of Thelsamar take with their barrels of blastpowder. Troggs have crept onto one of the islands too.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/The_Loch (largest body of water in Khaz Modan, threshadons)

title: Mo'grosh Stronghold
body: In the caves and hills of northeastern Loch Modan, across the water from Thelsamar, the Mo'grosh ogres have made their stronghold. Brutes, enforcers, shamans and mystics crowd the camp, and from here they raid the whole region: Thelsamar, the dam and the excavation site have all suffered, and an ore caravan bound from the Wetlands was ambushed and its cargo carried off. The ogres also mine crystals in their caves, a very rare commodity that anyone in need of one must take from them. The magistrate of Thelsamar has put a price on Chok'sul, the ogre presumed to lead them, and a brute called Emogg the Crusher is sometimes seen among them.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Mo'grosh_Stronghold (ogre-infested caves in northeastern Loch Modan; only this part used)

title: The Farstrider Lodge
body: In southeastern Loch Modan stands the Farstrider Lodge, a hunting lodge built in the high elven style, though only one elf still lives there. Its other residents are dwarven and human hunters, and Marek Ironheart, who leads them, prizes hunting skill above all else. Trainers, a bowyer and a gunsmith keep busy here, and hunters come from afar for the loch's famous crocolisks, whose skins and meat always find buyers. Buzzards nest in the hills nearby and great boars roam the meadows, giving the lodge's resident braggart, young Daryl the Youngling, endless excuses to challenge newcomers.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Farstrider_Lodge (high elven make, only one high elf, humans and dwarves, Marek Ironheart leader)
DB spawns in area 147: Dargh Trueaim, Claude Erksine, Cliff Hadin, Irene Sureshot, Daryl 1187, Vyrin 1156, Marek 1154

title: Ironband's Excavation Site
body: East of the loch, beyond its southern tip, Prospector Ironband of the Explorers' League leads a dig into ancient ruins. Work there has slowed to a crawl. Stonesplinter troggs have surfaced within the site itself and driven the dwarves out of the ruins, and some of them rage berserk among the pits. Trogg diggers and geomancers now overrun the excavation under Boss Galgosh, the Stonesplinter chieftain, and his tribal shaman Magosh. Ironband's camp clings to the edge of the site, waiting on blastpowder from Thelsamar and on anyone willing to fight.
sources: quest 436 description (ruins east of the lake, around the southern tip)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Ironband's_Excavation_Site (southeastern Loch Modan, troggs of a large and volatile breed drove prospectors out)
creature_template subnames 1398 Stonesplinter Chieftain, 1399 Stonesplinter Tribal Shaman
DB spawns in area 142: Stonesplinter Digger, Geomancer, Berserk Trogg, Ironband 1344, Fellhew 1345
notes: Converted: the idols and their effect on the troggs moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 297, Fellhew's quest, offered on the turn-in of 436). The troggs overrunning the site stay in the opening, since they stand in plain sight there. verified. Titan statue trivia left out (era unclear). Ironwing Cavern is Cataclysm.

parts.body: The troggs came up just after the diggers had uncovered a large number of strange carved idols in the ruins. The dwarves were chased away before they could study a single one, and the idols are now in trogg hands. Magmar Fellhew, who manages the site, says they have a strange effect on the creatures: they send them berserk.

title: Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII
body: Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII is the dwarf charged with the care of the Stonewrought Dam, and he takes that charge very seriously. The Dark Iron clan has already destroyed the Thandol Span and pillaged Dun Modr, and Hinderweir is certain the dam is next. Yet most of his security detail, his top inspector included, has been reassigned to the Alliance front, leaving him to watch for saboteurs with whatever help he can find. Dark Iron sappers have lately been seen milling about the dam's eastern ramp, and he wants someone to go and look for a clue.
notes: Converted: the barrel and the sample sent to Dun Modr moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 199); the seaforium, his remedy and the saving of the dam moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 283). Opening now ends on the sappers, the premise of quest 250. Hinderweir has no gossip; creature_text 1093 reread: period text. verified. Faction 1: Hinderweir uses faction template 55 (Ironforge), hostile to Horde, and quest 250 is Alliance only. His presumed death in the Cataclysm left out.

parts.body: The clue was a suspicious barrel near the sappers, full of a strange smelling powder. Hinderweir called it an alarming discovery and suspected an explosive at once. It had to be analyzed by an expert, so he sent a sample on a perilous journey through the Algaz Gate and across the Wetlands to Ashlan Stonesmirk, an explosives man assigned to the regiment at Dun Modr.

Ashlan named the powder seaforium, harmless while dry and ruinous once wet, and sent back a disarming colloid. Hinderweir mixed the remedy himself from lurker venom, a crocolisk tear and a crushed Mo'grosh crystal, just as Dark Iron insurgents planted a keg at the base of the dam. Stirred into the keg, it saved the Stonewrought Dam. Hinderweir called for three cheers, though he warns the dam is safe only for the time being.

title: Magistrate Bluntnose
body: Magistrate Bluntnose governs Thelsamar, and his patience with Ironforge is wearing thin. It took two months for word to come that a handful of soldiers might be spared for the town's defense, and he was told it would take two more for them to arrive. Meanwhile Thelsamar, the excavation and above all the dam lie open to attack. Bluntnose has done the practical thing and hired mercenaries, sending them against the ogres camped on the northeast of the lake, and he has posted a bounty on Chok'sul, the ogre presumed to lead them.
sources: quest 256 (by order of the Magistrate of Thelsamar)
notes: Converted: his plan to turn on the troggs once the ogres are dealt with (quest 255 reward text) moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 255). His reaction to Chok'sul's head is told in 3820 part 2. Per-ogre payment made general (quest 255 only says he hires arms). Faction 1: template 55 (Ironforge), Alliance-only quests.

parts.body: The hired arms did their work at the ogre camp, and Bluntnose was delighted, offering his thanks and those of all Thelsamar. If the ogre problem can be solved, he says, the town will at last be able to turn its attention to the troggs he curses so heartily.

title: Prospector Ironband
body: Prospector Ironband leads the Explorers' League dig east of the loch, a stout, honest dwarf who values results. Results have been hard to come by. Troggs have overrun his ruins, and his latest progress report to Thelsamar restates his request for more blastpowder. His concerns reach beyond his own site, too. Prospector Agmond, who has charge of the League's excavations in the Badlands to the southwest, has sent no word in weeks, and Ironband wants to know what has become of him.
sources: quest 436 description (stout, honest dwarf who values results)
quest 738 description (Agmond in charge of the Badlands sites, no word in weeks)
notes: Converted: Stormpike's curses and the missing load moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 301); the powder's arrival and the Dark Iron sympathizers to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 309). Agmond's death and the urns gave away the Badlands chain (badlands.json 331, which uses 738 and tells his fate and the urns): the opening keeps only the premise of 738, that Agmond has gone silent. The idols are told in 3812 part 1 and 3824 part 2 (Fellhew's quest 297). Faction 1: template 55. Wiki gives his first name as Darteus; not used. QUEST_DONE 298 hands his report to Jern; kept since 298 is his own quest. Check: report line trimmed to his latest report (quests 298, 436 reward), not a series.

parts.body: His report went all the way to Ironforge, where the hot-tempered Prospector Stormpike cursed Ironband's name. A load of blastpowder had been sent to him weeks ago, and the report made no mention of it. Where had it gone? Even so, Stormpike approved a fresh shipment, and wanted it watched every step of the way, since the last one never arrived.

The new powder reached Ironband at last, hauled in by the porter Miran under escort after a Dark Iron ambush on the road. Ironband was relieved, and troubled by the news that came with it: the Dark Irons have sympathizers able to get such material for their schemes. That, he decided, is a matter for someone else at some other time. He has powder to put to good use.

title: Captain Rugelfuss
body: Captain Rugelfuss commands the southern guard tower of Loch Modan, where his regiment watches over the gate and dares not leave it for fear of invasion. With the Ironforge Reserve called away to the Alliance front, he has a fraction of the soldiers he needs for the trogg war on his doorstep, so he relies on volunteers to carry the fight into the hills through his mountaineers Cobbleflint, Gravelgaw and Wallbang, keeping the troggs under pressure until reinforcements come. He asks for trogg stone teeth as proof of the work.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Loch_Modan (Rugelfuss sends dwarves against the troggs)
notes: Converted: the reinforcements that never came moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 237); the strike at Grawmug and its success to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 217). The opening keeps his hope of relief as an intention (quest 237 description). verified. Faction 1: template 55, Alliance-only quests.

parts.body: The reinforcements promised to the tower never showed. Word came back that the Alliance front had run red with the blood of fallen dwarves, and the news left a bitter taste at the tower. The mountaineers resolved that those deaths would not be for nothing, and pressed the trogg war all the harder.

In time the tower's scouts named the leader of the incursion, the chieftain Grawmug, and Rugelfuss sent a proven volunteer into Stonesplinter Valley to kill him and his guards Gnasher and Brawler. When it was done, the captain declared that hope had come to Loch Modan: with Grawmug dead, the dwarves stand a better chance of seeing the troggs driven from the land.

title: Daryl the Youngling
body: Daryl the Youngling, who much prefers to be called Daryl the Bold, is a young human hunter at the Farstrider Lodge with a great gift for boasting and very little for manners. He sets newcomers hunting challenges he is sure are beyond them, gets their names wrong, belittles every kill and is plainly astonished whenever they succeed. A scar runs over his eye, and he is always ready to offer the tale of how he came by it.
sources: quests 257, 258 descriptions, request and reward texts
quest 271 description (Vyrin's account of the scar)
notes: Converted: the true story of the scar moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 271, Vyrin's telling); the bear's head and his collapse to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 271, turned in to Daryl). Faction 1: template 55. He dates the scar to two years ago (quest 258) while Vyrin says a year (quest 271); no date given.

parts.body: Vyrin Swiftwind tells a less flattering version. The lodge's hunters had set their sights on a great bear called Ol' Sooty, and none of them had any luck. Daryl thought he would try his own hand against the beast, and all he had to show for it was the ugly scar over his eye.

When the head of Ol' Sooty was finally laid before him, Daryl's bravado collapsed. He ran a finger along his scar without thinking, muttered that it could not be that bear, then began to shake and begged for the grisly thing to be taken out of his sight.

title: Vyrin Swiftwind
body: Vyrin Swiftwind is the only high elf left at the Farstrider Lodge, a building of her people's make, and she greets visitors to it warmly. She has little patience for young Daryl's endless bragging. He does have some skill, she admits, though it pains her to say so, and what she would really like is a little payback for His Boldness, delivered by a hunter able enough to leave him speechless for once.
sources: quest 531 description and reward text (itching for months to get back at that snooty, stuck-up boy)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Farstrider_Lodge (high elven make, only one high elf)
notes: Converted: the scar story and her plan moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 271, her own quest); her satisfaction and 'he had it coming' to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 531, turned in to her). npc_text 3522, 3523, 3525 reread: classic text only. Faction 1: template 371 is hostile to Horde. Her marriage to Talithar comes from a 2012 novel and her Farstrider past is unclear in era, so both are left out.

parts.body: She knows the true story of his scar. Ol' Sooty, a bear every hunter at the lodge had failed to kill, marked Daryl when he tried his own luck. So Vyrin quietly recruits a capable hunter to slay the beast at its lair in the hills above Thelsamar and show the head to Daryl, and she can hardly wait to see his face.
sources: npc_text 3522 for 1156 (can't wait to see his face)

parts.body: The plan worked. Vyrin took the trophy off the hunter's hands, confessing she had been itching for months to get even with the haughty boy. Those who helped her are always welcome at the lodge, and she tells them not to worry about Daryl: he had it coming.

title: Bingles Blastenheimer
body: Bingles Blastenheimer is a gnome pilot who was sent to fly reconnaissance over Gnomeregan, the gnomish capital lost to troggs and leper gnomes. When he failed to report back for more than a week, his comrade Gnoarn in Ironforge was sure he had blown himself up. In truth he had crashed his gyrocopter into the loch, and troggs from a nearby island promptly made off with his tools and his special Blastencapper explosives. Stranded where he came down, Bingles has lost none of his zeal. He is convinced the movement to retake Gnomeregan depends on a gnomish air assault, and that it needs him.
sources: DB: Gnoarn 6569 starts 2039, spawned in Ironforge
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. Both triggers mean meeting Bingles, so his crash and the stolen tools stay in the opening. Comrades narrowed to Gnoarn (quest 2039 is his worry alone). ironforge.json 153713 uses QUEST_ACCEPT 2039 (at Gnoarn); this entry uses its turn-in at Bingles, a different trigger. Faction 1: template 55, Alliance-only quests.

title: Chok'sul
body: Chok'sul is the ogre whom the people of Thelsamar hold responsible for the raids on their town, the Stonewrought Dam and Ironband's excavation, presumed to be the leader who plans and coordinates the Mo'grosh attacks. By order of the magistrate a bounty has been posted on him, payable on proof of his death, and the wanted notice names him plainly. He keeps to the ogre camp in the northeast of Loch Modan, a brute who sizes up every intruder as a possible meal.
notes: Converted: the magistrate's reaction to the head moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 256); his death added as part 1 (KILL 1210 or QUEST_DONE 256), trimmed to what the kill tells. creature_text 1210 reread: battle cries only. verified. Faction 0: the KILL trigger is open to both factions (template 45 is hostile to all); QUEST_ACCEPT 256 is Alliance only.

parts.body: Chok'sul is dead, cut down at the ogre camp in the northeast of the loch. Whatever part he truly played in the raids on Thelsamar, the dam and the excavation, the Mo'grosh have lost the brute the magistrate named as their leader.

His head went back to Thelsamar as proof. Magistrate Bluntnose recoiled at the sight, demanding to know why anyone would bring such a thing to him, until he saw whose head it was. Then he was delighted, calling it quite a catch, and paid the bounty with the thanks of the whole town.

title: Grawmug
body: Grawmug is the chieftain of the Stonesplinter troggs, the leader that the scouts of the southern guard tower have found behind the trogg incursion into Loch Modan. He keeps to the depths of Stonesplinter Valley and never goes anywhere without his two elite guards, Gnasher and Brawler. Grawmug makes no secret of his ambitions. He greets intruders with promises to eat them for breakfast and proclaims that the Loch, and all the lands around it, now belong to the Stonesplinter tribe. Captain Rugelfuss believes that with Grawmug dead the troggs might at last be pushed back into the ground.
notes: Converted: opening unchanged (nothing to hide); his death added as part 1 (KILL 1205 or QUEST_DONE 217), trimmed to what the kill tells (his guards' fate is left to 3823). creature_text 1205 reread: battle cries only. verified. Faction 0: KILL trigger open to both; quest 217 Alliance only.

parts.body: Grawmug has fallen in the depths of Stonesplinter Valley. The chieftain who swore that the Loch belonged to the Stonesplinter tribe no longer leads the trogg incursion, and the dwarves of the southern guard tower hope that without him the troggs can be pushed back into the ground.

title: A Dark Threat Looms
body: With the Thandol Span destroyed and Dun Modr pillaged, Chief Engineer Hinderweir is sure the Stonewrought Dam will be the next target of the Dark Iron clan. The timing could hardly be worse. Most of the dam's security detail, his top inspector among them, has been reassigned to the Alliance front, and only a handful of mountaineers remain. Now Dark Iron sappers have been spotted milling about the dam's eastern ramp. Hinderweir is grateful that anyone cares for the dam's well-being at all, and asks a volunteer to investigate the area and bring back a clue to what the saboteurs intend.
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of quest 250 ('and he is right' dropped). Parts follow the chain: 1 the barrel and the journey to Dun Modr (QUEST_DONE 199, turned in to Hinderweir), 2 Ashlan names the seaforium (QUEST_ACCEPT 274, offered by Ashlan on the 161 turn-in; QuestType 2, flags 0), 3 the planted keg and the dam saved (QUEST_DONE 283). All seven quests are sorted under Loch Modan and no other file uses them. Ashlan (1073) stands in Dun Modr, so his TALK is not used here; wetlands.json has no entry or trigger for him yet (he is named only in the sources of 1109 Dun Modr). Faction 1: all quests Alliance only.

parts.body: Near the sappers sat a suspicious barrel full of a strange smelling powder. Hinderweir called it an alarming discovery and suspected some kind of explosive. It had to be analyzed by an expert, so he sent a sample on a grave and perilous journey through the Algaz Gate and along the road across the Wetlands to Ashlan Stonesmirk, assigned to the regiment guarding Dun Modr, with orders to stop for nothing.

Ashlan, whose ears still ring from his trade, knew the stuff at once by its tiny silver crystals and its smell: seaforium. Harmless while dry, once wet it could blow Ironforge out of its mountain. He sent back a disarming colloid, to be mixed with lurker venom, a crocolisk tear and a crushed Mo'grosh crystal, and urged that Hinderweir be told before it was too late.

The warning came none too soon. Dark Iron insurgents had swum a keg of the powder to the base of the dam with no mountaineers on hand to stop them. Hinderweir combined the ingredients into a disarming mixture, and once it was stirred into the keg the powder fizzled harmlessly. The Stonewrought Dam was saved, and it is safe again, Hinderweir says, for the time being at least.

title: In Defense of the King's Lands
body: With so many of King Magni's soldiers fighting on remote battlefields and the Ironforge Reserve called away to the Alliance front, the southern guard tower of Loch Modan must fight a trogg war with a fraction of the soldiers it needs, while troggs tunnel up from every crevice. Captain Rugelfuss cannot spare his regiment from the gate, so he turns to volunteers and asks for trogg teeth as proof of their work. Mountaineer Cobbleflint sends them against Stonesplinter troggs and scouts, Gravelgaw after the skullthumpers and seers of the southern hills, and Wallbang against the shamans and bonesnappers, all to keep the invaders under pressure until reinforcements arrive.
notes: Converted: the failed reinforcements moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 237, turned in to Gravelgaw); the strike at Grawmug to part 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 217, offered by Rugelfuss after 263); its success, a new part with the chain's ending, to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 217). Quest 267 stays an entry point (standalone). Faction 1: all quests Alliance only. verified

parts.body: No reinforcements came. The ones promised to the tower never showed, and the reason was grim: the fighting at the Alliance front had cost the dwarves dearly, and the field was crimson with the blood of their fallen. The mountaineers swallowed the bitter news and vowed those deaths would not go for naught. The volunteers in the hills were needed now more than ever.

At last the scouts identified the leader of the incursion: a chieftain named Grawmug, deep in Stonesplinter Valley and never without his two elite guards, Gnasher and Brawler. Rugelfuss chose to strike at the head of the invasion, entrusting a volunteer who had proven worthy with the assassination of all three.

Grawmug and both his guards were slain. Rugelfuss hailed the deed as hope brought to Loch Modan: with the trogg leadership dead, the dwarves stand a better chance of seeing the troggs driven from the land at last.

title: The Missing Blastpowder
body: Prospector Ironband's dig east of the loch has slowed to a crawl, despite all the supplies sent to him, and Jern Hornhelm of the Explorers' League in Thelsamar wants to know why. Ironband is a stout, honest dwarf who values results, and Jern worries that some force is at work against him. Magmar Fellhew, who manages the details of the site, should know the cause. Meanwhile Ironband has a progress report of his own to send back to Thelsamar, with a restated request for more blastpowder.
notes: Converted: the opening is the setup of quest 436 plus Ironband's report (298, a separate entry point). Parts: 1 the troggs (QUEST_DONE 436 or 298, both tell it), 2 the idols (QUEST_ACCEPT 297, offered by Fellhew on the 436 turn-in; the 298 route skips it), 3 the missing load and Stormpike's approval (QUEST_DONE 301), 4 the ambush and Saean's betrayal (QUEST_DONE 273, turned in to Huldar), 5 the powder delivered (QUEST_DONE 309). Saean (1380) has no spawn in this DB; he appears only in Huldar's account. npc_text 5494 (Huldar) and creature_text 1379 reread: classic text only. Faction 1: all quests Alliance only.

parts.body: The answer was troggs. Stonesplinter troggs have surfaced within the excavation and overrun it, holding up the work and leaving the dwarves to scrape along at the edge of their own dig. Whatever else is wrong at the site, that much is plain.

The troggs came up just after the diggers had uncovered a large number of strange carved idols. The dwarves were chased off before they could study them, the idols fell into trogg hands, and Fellhew is sure they are what drives the creatures berserk.

Ironband's report puzzled Jern, who had sent plenty of blastpowder weeks before. It had to go to Ironforge for approval, and there the hot-tempered Prospector Stormpike cursed Ironband: a load had gone to him weeks ago, and the report made no mention of it. Where had the powder gone? Stormpike approved a new shipment anyway, and wanted it watched personally every step of the way.

By then Huldar had already left Thelsamar with the porters Miran and Saean, following the curve of the loch. On the road they were ambushed by Dark Irons, and Saean, who had worked with them for almost a year, proved to be one of their sympathizers. Huldar never suspected him, and vowed it would take more than an ambush to stop the deliveries.

Miran hauled the rest of the barrels to the site under escort, braced for whatever else the Dark Irons had in store, and Ironband finally had his powder. Yet the news troubled him: the Dark Irons have sympathizers able to procure such material for their plans. Who supplies them is a question for another day.

title: The Ogre Menace
body: Thelsamar has waited months for help from Ironforge, and Magistrate Bluntnose is done waiting. The Mo'grosh ogres camped across the loch have raided the town, the dam and the excavation alike, so he hires mercenaries to cut down the ogres, brutes and enforcers. A wanted notice posted in town names the ogre presumed to lead them, Chok'sul, and promises payment for proof of his death. The ogres have taken more than lives. An ore caravan bound for Thelsamar from the Wetlands was ambushed by them, its last surviving guard dying of his wounds days later. That ore was meant for an alloy the smith Bailor Stonehand promised his old student Jordan Stilwell, and it must now be wrested back from the ogres' camp before the alloy can be made.
sources: page_text 873 (Jordan trained with Bailor, old teacher)
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. The Chok'sul bounty's end is told in 3820 parts 1 and 2. Dropped quest 1655 as a trigger (paladin only, step in the Stilwell class chain, not an entry point); its caravan facts kept as supported lore. Per-ogre pay made general.

title: Daryl the Bold
body: At the Farstrider Lodge, young Daryl, who styles himself Daryl the Bold, delights in testing newcomers. First he dares them to bring down buzzards against the clock, then elder mountain boars, sneering all the while, getting their names wrong and promising prizes he never expects to hand over. He likes to tell the story of his famous scar, too. Not everyone at the lodge is charmed. Vyrin Swiftwind, the lodge's high elf, would dearly like to see him humbled, and keeps an eye out for a hunter good enough to do it.
sources: npc_text for Vyrin 1156 (thanks for the laugh)
notes: Converted: the opening keeps Daryl's two challenges (257, 258) and Vyrin's wish to humble him. Parts: 1 the scar story (QUEST_ACCEPT 271), 2 the head shown to Daryl (QUEST_DONE 271, turned in to him), 3 Vyrin takes the trophy (QUEST_DONE 531, turned in to her). Faction 1: all quests Alliance only.

parts.body: Vyrin tells the real story of Daryl's scar. The lodge's hunters had failed to kill a great bear called Ol' Sooty, Daryl tried his own luck, and the bear marked him for it. She sends the hunter to Ol' Sooty's lair in the hills above Thelsamar, sure that the beast's head will leave even Daryl speechless.

It did. When the bear's head was laid before Daryl, he traced his scar without thinking and began to tremble, then begged for the grisly thing to be taken out of the lodge, stammering that it was not fit for anyone to see.

Vyrin gladly took the trophy off the hunter's hands and thanked them for the laugh. She had been waiting months to get even with the arrogant boy, and she counted it a job well done. Daryl, she says, had it coming.
